title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative: A comprehensive national employment policy (NEP) covering the period 2022-2026 was officially adopted in November 2022 with Government decision Nr. 785 (https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=134612&lang=ro). The NEP is aligned with international labour standards, builds on a solid labour market diagnostic, and is the results of the government and social partners engaging in tripartite dialogue on alternative policy options. As a result, the NEP tackles labour market exclusion, with a focus on inactive women and youth, enhancing working conditions, and safeguarding workers' rights. The NEP contains policy implementation provisions and a monitoring and evaluation framework. A Functional Assessment of the employment service agency of Moldova (ANOFM), conducted in April 2022, provided the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection with useful insights on the institutional capacities of ANOFM to deliver key NEP objectives, including through more effective active labour market policies. It also identified short- and medium-term pathways towards the modernization of the agency. Through RBSA, the ILO provided technical assistance to the constituents during the formulation of the national employment policy (NEP) and in conducting the Functional Assessment of the employment agency. This included the elaboration of the labour market diagnostic, the preparation of the functional assessment in line with the ILO methodology, and a series of capacity development events for tripartite constituents on the design and implementation of a human-centred and gender-transformative employment policy. With the support of Switzerland’s State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), the ILO supported the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection and the employment agency in the implementation of priority interventions foreseen in the NEP.

description.narrative:
A model for the award of microcredentials in one priority economic sector has been designed in 2023, in consultation with the social partners and the Ministries of Education and Labour. The model lays out the necessary institutional arrangements and mechanisms for awarding microcredentials and allows for more effective and labour market responsive adult re-skilling and upskilling programmes to boost employability, in particular of low skilled adults.
A gender-sensitive and inclusive pilot programme on digital literacy for disadvantaged adult populations has been designed in 2023, in consultation with the Ministry of Education and the social partners. The programme lays out the contents, methodologies and inter-institutional arrangements to equip low-skilled, excluded adults, in particular in rural areas, with digital core employability and life skills. It includes a gender lense and a disability focus, as well as concrete recommendations for reaching disadvantaged adults. With the support of the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), the ILO developed a.) a report with concrete recommendations on how to identify microcredentials and design related certifications and training programmes b.) a proposal for a training programme on digital literacy, delineating learning objectives, contents, methodologies and results, as well as institutional arrangements for implementation and for the inclusion of women and disadvantaged learners.

Output 3.2. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative: In Moldova, the model of Local Employment Partnerships (LEPs), which enables the decentralized implementation of the new national employment policy (NEP, 2022-2026) and the operationalization of decent work measures in rural areas, has expanded to other regions of the country through innovative strategies geared towards enhancing the labour market inclusion of young people not in education employment and training (NEET) living in rural areas. LEPs in Soroca and Rezina started their operations in November 2022 leading to the identification of more than 2400 young NEETs (of which 1385 women) who were referred to the employment agency for further support in transitioning to the labour market. Of these, 420 individuals received entrepreneurial and technical training with 150 starting new businesses and over 260 found a new job. The LEP’s new focus on outreach is particularly important in rural areas, where young people and women often do not have access to quality employment services. Through the LEPs in these two regions, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection has initiated the implementation of outreach strategies to young NEETs in rural areas, as provided by art. 29 of L105/2018, and has designed new by-laws on outreach. Furthermore, with a view to improve the targeting of beneficiaries, it has introduced the practice of territorial audits (a local labour market profile) to be routinely conducted by the Labour Market Observatory of the National Employment Agency (the order of the NEA will be published before the end of the year and we can put the link here). The tripartite territorial committees for consultation and collective bargaining (TCCCB) have played a significant role in the expansion of Local Entrepreneurial Partnerships (LEPs)the. Comprising local government representatives, social partners, and other key stakeholders, these committees operate across all 12 districts of Moldova and are key for the sustainability of the LEP process in Moldova. Through RBSA, the ILO offered capacity development and training opportunities to the tripartite territorial committees for consultation and collective bargaining (TCCCB) operating in the 12 districts of the country on design, implementation, and monitoring of Local Employment Partnerships (LEPs). This has allowed the TCCCB to analyze the data of the territorial audits conducted and identify the groups most at risk of labour market exclusion in their region. LEPs are then designed and implemented to tackle these specific barriers to decent work. During the reporting period, technical and financial support was extended to the design and implementation of two LEPs with a focus on creating decent work opportunities in the rural areas of the country. With the support of Switzerland’s State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), the ILO facilitated the design of two additional LEPs during the last quarter of 2023.
